questions.question: Which of the following organs represents the female reproductive part of a flower in angiosperms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gynoecium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gynoecium** is the **female reproductive organ** of a flower in angiosperms. It consists of one or more carpels, which are the structural units of the gynoecium.
 
• The gynoecium includes three main parts: **ovary, style, and stigma**.
 
 
• The **ovary** contains ovules, which develop into seeds after fertilization.
 
• The **style** is a tube-like structure connecting the stigma to the ovary.
 
• The **stigma** is the receptive surface for pollen grains during pollination.
 
 
 
• The gynoecium plays a vital role in **sexual reproduction** by facilitating pollination, fertilization, and seed development.
 
• It is a defining feature of angiosperms, helping ensure **successful reproduction** and species propagation.
 
• Other parts of a flower, such as petals, stamens, and androecium, have different roles and are not involved in female reproduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Petal:**

 
 
• Petals are the colorful, often fragrant parts of a flower that attract pollinators such as bees and butterflies.
 
• They do not contribute directly to reproduction but play a supportive role in pollination.
 
 
 
• **Androecium:**
 
 
• The androecium is the male reproductive organ of a flower, consisting of stamens.
 
• Each stamen has two parts: the anther (produces pollen) and the filament.
 
 
 
• **Stamen:**
 
 
• Stamens are part of the androecium and are responsible for producing and dispersing pollen grains.
 
• They facilitate male gamete transfer to the stigma of the gynoecium.
 
 
 
• **Female Reproductive Process in Flowers:**
 
 
• Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma.
 
• Fertilization occurs when male gametes from pollen unite with ovules in the ovary.
 
• After fertilization, ovules develop into seeds, and the ovary matures into a fruit.
 
 
 
• **Angiosperms:**
 
 
• Angiosperms are flowering plants that reproduce sexually through their reproductive organs (androecium and gynoecium).
 
• They are the most diverse group of plants, containing over 300,000 species.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pollination and Fertilization:**

 
 
• Pollination can be either **self-pollination** (within the same flower or plant) or **cross-pollination** (between different plants).
 
• Fertilization results in the formation of a **zygote**, which develops into an embryo and eventually a seed.
 
 
 
• **Fruit Formation:**
 
 
• The ovary develops into a fruit, protecting the seeds and aiding in their dispersal.
 
• Fruits can be classified as simple, aggregate, or multiple based on their development.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Importance:**
 
 
• Flowering plants dominate terrestrial ecosystems due to their efficient reproductive strategies.
 
• The gynoecium ensures genetic diversity and species survival through sexual reproduction.

questions.question: In a plant cell, the act of respiration to take in oxygen and release energy and carbon dioxide from food occurs in the _________ .
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mitochondria are known as the **powerhouses of the cell** because they generate most of the cell’s supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• In plant cells, mitochondria are the primary site of cellular respiration, where oxygen is used to convert nutrients into energy.
 
• During respiration, mitochondria **take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide** and energy in the form of ATP.
 
• They have their own DNA, which is separate from the nuclear DNA, and can replicate independently within the cell.
 
• The process of cellular respiration in mitochondria occurs in three main stages: glycolysis, the citric acid cycle, and the electron transport chain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peroxisomes**: Organelles that contain enzymes for oxidative reactions, important in the metabolism of fatty acids and the detoxification of harmful substances.
 
• **Chloroplasts**: Organelles found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae that conduct photosynthesis, where light energy is converted into chemical energy stored in glucose.
 
• **Vacuoles**: Large vesicles in plant cells that store nutrients, waste products, and help maintain turgor pressure against the cell wall.
 
• **Electron Transport Chain**: A series of protein complexes within the inner mitochondrial membrane that transfer electrons from electron donors to electron acceptors via redox reactions, coupled with the transfer of protons (H+ ions) across the membrane.
 
• **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)**: The main energy currency of the cell, providing energy for various cellular processes, including muscle contraction, nerve impulse propagation, and chemical synthesis.

questions.question: By which process the water evaporates through the stomata present on the surface of the leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Transpiration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Transpiration** is the process by which water evaporates from the aerial parts of plants, primarily through the stomata on the leaves.
 
• It helps in the **regulation of temperature** in plants and maintains the flow of water and nutrients from the roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• Approximately **90% of water absorbed by plants** is lost through transpiration, indicating its critical role in plant physiology.
 
• Transpiration also creates a suction force called the **transpiration pull**, which helps in the upward movement of water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the leaves.
 
• The rate of transpiration is influenced by environmental factors such as light, temperature, humidity, and wind.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis**

 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose and oxygen.
 
• The reaction occurs in the **chloroplasts** of plant cells, containing the green pigment chlorophyll.
 
• This process is essential for producing the food required by plants and indirectly sustains most life on Earth by producing oxygen.
 
• It is represented by the equation: **6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2**.
 
 
 
• **Transportation**
 
 
• Transportation in plants refers to the movement of water, minerals, and nutrients throughout the plant body.
 
• The **xylem** is responsible for transporting water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant, while the **phloem** transports food (sugar) from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• This process is crucial for maintaining plant growth, repair, and reproduction.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation**
 
 
• Evaporation is the process of converting liquid water into water vapor due to heat energy.
 
• Unlike transpiration, evaporation occurs from any exposed surface, such as soil, water bodies, or other non-living surfaces.
 
• It plays a key role in the **water cycle**, helping to transfer moisture from the Earth's surface to the atmosphere.

W = mg

Where m is the mass of the body and g is the acceleration due to gravity.

 
• Weightlessness: Weightlessness is a sensation experienced by a body in the absence of any forces of gravity acting on it.

EXPLANATION__:

• Thus in the spacecraft, everything inside it is in a state of **free fall**.
 
• When an object is in free fall, it is **weightless **as there is **no upward force** to counteract the gravitational force.
 
• Hence, an **object under freefall experiences weightlessness.**
 
• Therefore, the **weightlessness experienced by objects in a spacecraft orbiting** the earth is due to the** freefall of the spacecraft.**

questions.question: Myopia is also known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Near sightedness.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Myopia (or short-sightedness)** is a defect of vision due to which a person cannot see the** distant objects clearly** (though he can see the nearby objects clearly).
 
• The far point of an eye suffering from myopia is less than infinity.
 
• Such a person can see clearly only up to a distance of few meters.
 
• Myopia (short-sightedness or near-sightedness) is corrected by using spectacles containing concave lenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ability to see is called vision.
 
• There are three common defects of vision (or defects of the eye).
 
• These are 
 
 
• **Myopia (Short-sightedness or Near-sightedness)**
 
• **Hypermetropia (Long-sightedness or Far-sightedness)**
 
 
• Hypermetropia (or long-sightedness) is a defect of vision due to which a person cannot see the nearby objects clearly (though he can see the distant objects clearly).
 
• The near-point of a hypermetropic eye is more than 25 centimeters away.
 
• Hypermetropia (long-sightedness or far-sightedness) is corrected by using spectacles containing convex lenses
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**
 
 
• Presbyopia is a defect of vision due to which an old person cannot see the nearby objects clearly due to loss of power of accommodation of the eye.
 
• The near-point of the old person having presbyopia gradually recedes and becomes much more than 25 centimeters away.
 
• Presbyopia defect is corrected in the same way as hypermetropia by using spectacles having convex lenses.

questions.question: Jitin's age 3 years from now will be double the average of Jitin's current age and his age 8 years ago. What was Jitin's age 5 years ago?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Double the **average** of two values is always equal to their **sum**.

Age 3 years from now = (**Current age**) + (**Age 8 years ago**)

Current age + 3 = Current age + (Current age − 8)

3 = Current age − 8 ⇒ **Current age** = 11 years.

Jitin's age 5 years ago = 11 − 5 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let **Jitin's current age** be J.

Age 3 years from now = J + 3

Age 8 years ago = J − 8

**Formula Used:**

Average of two numbers A and B = (A + B) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe0bfdf3fd88f60927e7c16c198e2c7627db092978fd3dfcb3f5144a4ff7952c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average of current age and age 8 years ago = [J + (J − 8)] ÷ 2

⇒ Average = (2J − 8) ÷ 2 = J − 4

⇒ According to the question: (J + 3) = 2 × (J − 4)

⇒ J + 3 = 2J − 8

⇒ 2J − J = 8 + 3

⇒ J = 11 years

⇒ Jitin's age 5 years ago = J − 5 = 11 − 5 = 6 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Representation of Ages

If the current age is x, then age after n years is (x + n) and age n years ago was (x − n).

Average of Ages

The average of ages of n people is the sum of their individual ages divided by n.

Ratio and Proportions in Ages

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant throughout their lives, which is a key property for solving ratio-based age problems.</p

questions.question: Find the sum of the numbers between 550 and 700 such that when they are divided by 12, 16 and 24, leave remainder 5 in each case.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Common divisor = **LCM**(12, 16, 24) = 48.

Numbers are of form **48k + 5**.

For range 550 − 700: k = 12 (581), k = 13 (629), k = 14 (677).

Sum = 581 + 629 + 677 = 1887.

**∴ The correct answer is 1887.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1f48bbb2c97ef02b5356cad106ae7e88b282cddeecef97cd6a3e9d9f462ea573.png] 

**Given:** Divisors are 12, 16, and 24. Remainder in each case is 5. Range is 550 to 700.

**Formula:** Number = **LCM(divisors) × k + remainder**

⇒ LCM(12, 16, 24):

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3, 16 = 2⁴, 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3 = 16 × 3 = 48

⇒ General form = 48k + 5

⇒ If k = 12, Number = 48 × 12 + 5 = 576 + 5 = 581

⇒ If k = 13, Number = 48 × 13 + 5 = 624 + 5 = 629

⇒ If k = 14, Number = 48 × 14 + 5 = 672 + 5 = 677

⇒ If k = 15, Number = 48 × 15 + 5 = 720 + 5 = 725 (Outside range)

⇒ Sum = 581 + 629 + 677 = 1887

**∴ The correct answer is 1887.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method for Remainders

When a number leaves the same remainder 'r' when divided by x, y, and z, the number is of the form **LCM(x, y, z)k + r**.

Arithmetic Progression Sum

If the found numbers form an AP, the sum can also be calculated as **n/2 × (first term + last term)**.

Different Remainders

If remainders are different such that (divisor − remainder) = constant (d), then the number is **LCM(divisors)k − d**.</p

questions.question: If sec θ - cos θ = 14 and 14 sec θ = x, then the value of x is _________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: 14 = **sec θ − cos θ**

Substitute 14 in the second equation: x = (**sec θ − cos θ**) × **sec θ**

⇒ x = sec² θ − (cos θ × sec θ)

⇒ x = sec² θ − 1 = tan² θ

**∴ The correct answer is tan² θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sec θ − cos θ = 14 and 14 sec θ = x

**Formula Used:** sec θ × cos θ = 1; sec² θ − 1 = tan² θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/662d6979d84d4eda985eee5577d276a7d24924326b4ebd1cd3a7f6010a393b03.png] 

⇒ From the first equation, we have 14 = sec θ − cos θ

⇒ Substitute the value of 14 in the second equation: x = (sec θ − cos θ) × sec θ

⇒ x = sec² θ − (cos θ × sec θ)

⇒ Since cos θ × sec θ = 1, we get x = sec² θ − 1

⇒ Using identity sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, x = tan² θ

**∴ The correct answer is tan² θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental square relations: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

The product of a trigonometric ratio and its reciprocal is always 1: sinθ × cosecθ = 1, cosθ × secθ = 1, and tanθ × cotθ = 1.</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 1,727 is divided into three parts A, B and C so that their amounts after 3, 4 and 5 years, respectively, are equal, the rate of simple interest being 5% per annum. How much is A?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of parts when amounts are equal = 1/(100 + R₁T₁) : 1/(100 + R₂T₂) : 1/(100 + R₃T₃)

Ratio A : B : C = 1/(100 + 5×3) : 1/(100 + 5×4) : 1/(100 + 5×5) = 1/115 : 1/120 : 1/125

Simplified Ratio = 1/23 : 1/24 : 1/25 = (24×25) : (23×25) : (23×24) = 600 : 575 : 552

Total units = 600 + 575 + 552 = 1727 units → Rs. 1,727, so 1 unit = Rs. 1

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total Sum = Rs. 1,727, Rate (R) = 5% per annum, Time for A (T₁) = 3 years, Time for B (T₂) = 4 years, Time for C (T₃) = 5 years.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P × (1 + RT/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/002b55141efdc3aac1340e04f281f6f407c817c956a283a4db9297bf2f46bc9c.png] 

⇒ Amount A = A × (1 + 5 × 3 / 100) = 1.15A

⇒ Amount B = B × (1 + 5 × 4 / 100) = 1.20B

⇒ Amount C = C × (1 + 5 × 5 / 100) = 1.25C

⇒ 1.15A = 1.20B = 1.25C ⇒ 115A = 120B = 125C

⇒ 23A = 24B = 25C

⇒ A : B : C = (1/23) : (1/24) : (1/25) = (24 × 25) : (23 × 25) : (23 × 24)

⇒ A : B : C = 600 : 575 : 552

⇒ Sum of ratio = 600 + 575 + 552 = 1727

⇒ Share of A = (600 / 1727) × 1727 = Rs. 600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

Interest (I) = (P × R × T) / 100, where P is principal, R is rate, and T is time.

Case of Equal Interests

If the Simple Interests are equal, the principal parts are divided in the ratio P₁ : P₂ : P₃ = 1/R₁T₁ : 1/R₂T₂ : 1/R₃T₃.

Case of Equal Amounts

If the Amounts are equal, the principal parts are divided in the ratio P₁ : P₂ : P₃ = 1/(100 + R₁T₁) : 1/(100 + R₂T₂) : 1/(100 + R₃T₃).</p

questions.question: The ratio of the age of A : C = 1 : 2, C : D = 2 : 3 and B : C = 5 : 6. If the difference in the age of B and D is 28, then find the average age of A and B.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine ratios **A : C : D** = 1 : 2 : 3 and **B : C** = 5 : 6.

To equalize **C**, multiply **A : C : D** by 3 → **A : B : C : D** = 3 : 5 : 6 : 9.

Difference between **D** and **B** = 9 − 5 = 4 units = **28 years** → 1 unit = **7 years**.

Average of **A** and **B** = (3 + 5) ÷ 2 = 4 units → 4 × 7 = **28 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratios **A : C** = 1 : 2, **C : D** = 2 : 3, and **B : C** = 5 : 6. Age difference **D − B** = 28.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21490db25cde7c0ebd09127316e1b4912e786c6578c419d00629f3d468a6f6ca.png] 

⇒ Combining ratios: **A : C : D** = 1 : 2 : 3.

⇒ To link **B : C** (5 : 6), multiply **A : C : D** by 3: **A : C : D** = 3 : 6 : 9.

⇒ Combined Ratio **A : B : C : D** = 3 : 5 : 6 : 9.

⇒ Difference between **D** and **B**: 9x − 5x = 4x.

⇒ 4x = 28 ⇒ x = 7.

⇒ Average age of **A** and **B** = (3x + 5x) ÷ 2 = 8x ÷ 2 = 4x.

⇒ Average age = 4 × 7 = 28 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Balancing

To combine ratios like **a:b** and **b:c**, multiply the ratios by factors such that the common term **b** has the same value in both.

Average of Ratios

The average of two quantities represented as **mx** and **nx** is calculated as **(m + n)x ÷ 2**, provided they share the same common variable.

Age Difference Property

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant regardless of the number of years passed or the current reference point.</p

questions.question: In a triangle ABC sides AB = 28 cm, BC = 32 cm and AC = 20 cm. AD is the angle bisector of ∠A on BC and AM is the median of the same side. The distance between the foot of median and the foot of angle bisector is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By standard formula, the distance between the foot of the median and the foot of the angle bisector on side **BC** is given by:

**DM = |(BC ÷ 2) − [AB × BC ÷ (AB + AC)]|**

Substitute the given values: **AB = 28 cm**, **AC = 20 cm**, and **BC = 32 cm**:

⇒ DM = |16 − [28 × 32 ÷ 48]|

⇒ DM = |16 − 56/3| = 8/3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8/3 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of triangle ABC: **AB = 28 cm**, **BC = 32 cm**, and **AC = 20 cm**.

**AD** is the angle bisector of ∠A on BC and **AM** is the median to BC.

**Formula Used:**

1. Midpoint property: **BM = MC = BC ÷ 2**

2. Angle Bisector Theorem: **BD ÷ DC = AB ÷ AC**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/353282711257dc3999d6a5ba5055051fe1e34779d8eab2bdcf68ac04500a5a2f.png] 

**Calculations:**

Since **AM** is the median to **BC**, **M** is the midpoint of **BC**:

⇒ BM = BC ÷ 2

⇒ BM = 32 ÷ 2 = 16 cm

According to the **Angle Bisector Theorem**, the bisector **AD** divides the opposite side **BC** in the ratio of the other two sides **AB** and **AC**:

⇒ BD ÷ DC = AB ÷ AC

⇒ BD ÷ DC = 28 ÷ 20 = 7 ÷ 5

Let BD = 7k and DC = 5k.

⇒ BD + DC = BC

⇒ 7k + 5k = 32

⇒ 12k = 32

⇒ k = 32 ÷ 12 = 8/3

Now, find the length of **BD**:

⇒ BD = 7 × (8/3) = 56/3 cm

The distance between the foot of the median (**M**) and the foot of the angle bisector (**D**) is **DM**:

⇒ DM = BD − BM

⇒ DM = 56/3 − 16

⇒ DM = (56 − 48) ÷ 3

⇒ DM = 8/3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8/3 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Theorem

An angle bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side into two segments that are proportional to the other two sides of the triangle.

Median of a Triangle

A median of a triangle is a line segment joining a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, thus bisecting that side into two equal halves.

Length of Angle Bisector (Stewart's Theorem)

The length of the angle bisector AD can be calculated using the formula: AD² = AB × AC − BD × DC.</p

questions.question: P is a point on line AB and PQ is a ray such that ∠QPA = 7x and ∠QPB = 5x. Then, the value of (8x - 10°) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of angles on a **straight line** (Linear Pair) = 180°

Sum of ratio components = 7x + 5x = 12x

12x = 180° ⇒ x = 15°

Required value = (8 × 15°) − 10°

Required value = 120° − 10° = 110°

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠QPA = 7x and ∠QPB = 5x

**Formula Used:** Sum of **Linear Pair** of angles = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d4c23a8253295fdb6142a608af248665c2719518f93ee31b1bfbf86add1e170.png] 

Since AB is a **straight line** and PQ is a ray starting from P on AB:

⇒ ∠QPA + ∠QPB = 180°

⇒ 7x + 5x = 180°

⇒ 12x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 12

⇒ x = 15°

To find the value of (8x − 10°):

⇒ (8 × 15°) − 10°

⇒ 120° − 10°

⇒ 110°

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a line, then the sum of the two adjacent angles so formed is 180°. Such angles are called **supplementary angles**.

Straight Angle

An angle whose measure is exactly 180° is called a **straight angle**, which forms a perfectly straight line.

Adjacent Angles

Two angles are **adjacent** if they have a common vertex and a common arm, but no common interior points.</p

questions.question: If the expression x³ + 3x² + 4x + k has a factor x + 5, then what is the value of k?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If (x + 5) is a factor, then substituting x = −5 must make the expression zero.

Expression: (−5)³ + 3(−5)² + 4(−5) + k = 0

−125 + 3(25) − 20 + k = 0

−145 + 75 + k = 0 ⇒ k − 70 = 0

k = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Polynomial P(x) = x³ + 3x² + 4x + k and a factor (x + 5).

Formula Used: Factor Theorem states that if (x + a) is a factor of P(x), then P(−a) = 0.

⇒ Let the factor be x + 5 = 0, which gives x = −5.

⇒ Substitute x = −5 into the polynomial P(x):

⇒ P(−5) = (−5)³ + 3(−5)² + 4(−5) + k = 0

⇒ −125 + 3(25) − 20 + k = 0

⇒ −125 + 75 − 20 + k = 0

⇒ (−125 − 20) + 75 + k = 0

⇒ −145 + 75 + k = 0

⇒ −70 + k = 0

⇒ k = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Additional Information__**

Factor Theorem

A polynomial f(x) has a factor (x − a) if and only if f(a) = 0. This is a special case of the remainder theorem.

Remainder Theorem

When a polynomial f(x) is divided by a linear divisor (x − a), the remainder of the division is f(a).

Synthetic Division

A shorthand method of polynomial division, especially when dividing by a linear factor of the form (x − a).

Roots of Polynomials

If x = r is a root of P(x) = 0, then (x − r) is exactly divisible by P(x), meaning the remainder is zero.</p

questions.question: A person sold an article for Rs. 3,600 and got a profit of 20%. Had he sold the article for Rs. 3,150, how much profit would he have got?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit 20% means **Selling Price** is 120% of **Cost Price**.

120% → Rs. 3,600

1% → 3,600 ÷ 120 = Rs. 30

New Selling Price Rs. 3,150 → 3,150 ÷ 30 = 105%

**New Profit%** = 105% − 100% = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial SP = Rs. 3,600, Profit = 20%, New SP = Rs. 3,150.
**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + P%) | Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0d98a12cacb7a8282ce59cb4dc4b11006fc500653d33e2bc7da83235539837b.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 3,600 × 100 ÷ (100 + 20) = 3,600 × 100 ÷ 120 = **Rs. 3,000**

⇒ **New Selling Price (SP)** = Rs. 3,150

⇒ **New Profit** = New SP − CP = 3,150 − 3,000 = **Rs. 150**

⇒ **New Profit%** = (150 ÷ 3,000) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise. If SP > CP, it is profit; if CP > SP, it is loss.

Fractional Conversion

20% profit can be written as 1/5. This means if **CP is 5 units**, **Profit is 1 unit**, and **SP is 6 units**.</p

questions.question: The certain sum will amount to Rs 33640 in 2 years at 16% per annum of compound interest, interest being compounded annually. The sum is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate of interest 16% = 4/25 in fraction form.

Ratio of **Principal** to **Amount** for 1 year = 25 : (25 + 4) = 25 : 29.

For 2 years, the ratio becomes 25² : 29² = 625 : 841.

Given 841 units = ₹ 33640 → 1 unit = 33640 ÷ 841 = ₹ 40.

**Principal** = 625 units × 40 = ₹ 25000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 25000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount (A)** = ₹ 33640

**Rate (R)** = 16% per annum

**Time (n)** = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5003877ceb350c801e051de6b0a28f72df804d6da051cbffa15892ebbf66c6f5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 33640 = P(1 + 16/100)²

⇒ 33640 = P(1 + 4/25)²

⇒ 33640 = P(29/25)²

⇒ 33640 = P × (841 / 625)

⇒ P = (33640 × 625) ÷ 841

⇒ P = 40 × 625

⇒ P = 25000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 25000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years at rate R%, the effective interest rate is R + R + (R×R)/100. In this case, 16 + 16 + 2.56 = 34.56%.

Difference between CI and SI

Compound Interest Formula

CI = Amount − Principal = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1].

questions.question: Find the volume of a cylinder whose base radius is 12.5 cm and whose height is (4)/(5) of the base radius.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Height** (h) = 4/5 × 12.5 = 10 cm

**Given:**

Base **radius** (r) = 12.5 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38b12a1b6939087ceb8d70f2e7ff7a9768ad65fbe0d3b35c76805ea42351e50f.png] 

**Calculations:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

questions.question: The average speed of the car is 16 km/hr during the whole journey. If the first half of the journey is covered at 40 km/hr, then find the speed with which the car covers the second half of the journey. (in km/hr)

questions.question: ABC is an isosceles triangle in which AB = AC and ∠*BAC* = 50°. Side BC is extended to D. Find the measure of ∠*ACD*.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **isosceles triangle** with **AB = AC**, base angles ∠ABC and ∠ACB are equal.

Base angles = (180° − 50°) ÷ 2 = 65°.

The **exterior angle** ∠ACD is equal to the sum of the two opposite **interior angles**.

∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC = 50° + 65° = 115°.

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **AB = AC** and ∠BAC = 50° in **▵ABC**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in a **triangle** is 180°; **Linear pair** sum is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2842ee79687b82aa3f9f3b6cf70788dfd57b08f9b6b0d5f62a4fc064b3c9db1.png] 

In **▵ABC**, since **AB = AC**:

⇒ ∠ABC = ∠ACB (Angles opposite to equal sides are equal)

⇒ ∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ 50° + 2 × ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠ACB = 180° − 50° = 130°

⇒ ∠ACB = 65°

Side **BC** is extended to **D**, forming a **linear pair** at point **C**:

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ACD = 180°

⇒ 65° + ∠ACD = 180°

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − 65° = 115°

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is always equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles of the triangle.

Isosceles Triangle Property

If two sides of a triangle are equal, then the angles opposite to those sides are also equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.</p

questions.question: If the length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and the breadth is decreased by 20%, then the percentage increase or decreases in the area of the rectangle is -

Use the **successive percentage change** formula: Net Change = x + y + (x × y)/100.

questions.question: The ratio of new expenditure to that of the initial expenditure is 15 : 16. If the price of petrol is increased by 25% then the consumption of petrol is decreased by x%. Find the value of x.

**Ratio** of **Expenditure** (New : Initial) = 15 : 16

**Price** increase of 25% → **Ratio** of **Price** (New : Initial) = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4

**Consumption Ratio** = (Expenditure Ratio) ÷ (Price Ratio) = (15/5) : (16/4) = 3 : 4

**Decrease** in **Consumption** = (4 − 3) ÷ 4 × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

⇒ x = (0.04 ÷ 0.16) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%

3 **Notebooks** = 125% of 4 **Pens** ⇒ 3N = (5/4) × 4P ⇒ 3N = 5P ⇒ Ratio N : P = 5 : 3.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding National Science Day:

I. It is celebrated every year on 22 February to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sir C.V. Raman.

II. Sir C.V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for the discovery of the Raman Effect.

III. The National Science Day 2026 theme is "Science and Technology for a Sustainable Future".

Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I and III only.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__Analysis of Statements__**

__
 
• **Statement I is Incorrect:** National Science Day is celebrated on **28 February** (not 22 February). Furthermore, it does not commemorate his birth anniversary; it commemorates the date he **discovered the Raman Effect** in 1928. (His birthday is actually November 7).
 
• **Statement II is Correct:** Sir C.V. Raman was indeed awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930**. He was the first Indian and first Asian to receive a Nobel Prize in any scientific branch.
 
• **Statement III is inorrect:** The theme for 2026 is **"Women in Science: Catalysing Viksit Bharat"**, which highlights the role of women scientists in reaching the goal of a developed India by 2047.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **The Raman Effect__**

__
 
• It refers to the **inelastic scattering of photons** by matter, meaning there is an exchange of energy and a change in the light's direction.
 
• When a beam of light traverses a dust-free, transparent sample of a chemical compound, a small fraction of the light emerges in directions other than that of the incident (incoming) beam.
 
• Most of this scattered light is of unchanged wavelength. However, a small part has wavelengths different from that of the incident light; its presence is a result of the **Raman Effect**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Quick Facts for Revision__**

Consider the following statements regarding the Global Hunger Index 2025:

 
• India is ranked 102nd in the Global Hunger Index 2025.
 
• India falls under the “Moderate” hunger category.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1: **India is ranked 102nd out of 123 countries in the Global Hunger Index 2025. This statement is correct.
 
• Statement 2: This statement is incorrect, because according to recent Global Hunger Index reports, India falls under the “Serious” hunger category, not Moderate.
 
• The **Global Hunger Index (GHI)** is a tool that measures and tracks hunger globally, regionally, and by country. It calculates hunger levels based on four indicators: **undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting, and child mortality.**
 
• The GHI rankings are published annually, and India's performance has been closely observed due to its large population and persistent challenges in nutrition and food security.
 
• *Hence, both statements provided in the question are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Hunger Index:**

 
 
• The GHI is jointly published by **Concern Worldwide** and **Welthungerhilfe**, two organizations working towards ending global hunger.
 
• The index uses four indicators to calculate hunger levels: **undernourishment, child wasting (low weight for height), child stunting (low height for age), and child mortality.**
 
• The GHI categorizes countries into five levels of hunger: **low, moderate, serious, alarming, and extremely alarming.**
 
• India has consistently ranked in the "Serious" category in recent years, highlighting ongoing challenges in addressing malnutrition, food insecurity, and child health.
 
 
 
• **Key Indicators of Hunger:**
 
 
• **Undernourishment:** Refers to the insufficient caloric intake of a population.
 
• **Child Wasting:** Indicates acute malnutrition where children are underweight for their height.
 
• **Child Stunting:** Represents chronic malnutrition where children are shorter than expected for their age.
 
• **Child Mortality:** Refers to deaths of children under five years, often linked to malnutrition and poor health services.
 
 
 
• **Efforts to Address Hunger in India:**
 
 
• The Government of India has implemented several schemes to address hunger and malnutrition, such as the **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), Mid-Day Meal Scheme, and Poshan Abhiyaan.**
 
• The **National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013** aims to provide subsidized food grains to approximately 67% of India's population.
 
• Despite these efforts, challenges persist in implementation and coverage, necessitating further improvements.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Hunger Index Thresholds:**

 
 
• A score below 9.9 is categorized as "low hunger," while scores between 10 and 19.9 are "moderate hunger."
 
• Scores between 20 and 34.9 are "serious hunger," 35 to 49.9 are "alarming hunger," and above 50 are "extremely alarming hunger."
 
• India’s recent GHI scores place it firmly in the "serious" category.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Addressing Hunger:**
 
 
• Poverty, lack of education, and inadequate health services contribute to persistent hunger in India.
 
• Natural disasters, climate change, and economic challenges further exacerbate food insecurity.
 
• Targeted policies and efficient implementation are crucial to reduce hunger and malnutrition across the country.

questions.question: According to the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, which of the following is NOT one of the five stages involved in the approach to estimating monetisation potential?

options.text: Direct permanent sale of public land to private developers
Determination of the most suitable mode of monetisation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Direct permanent sale of public land to private developers.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 Launch:** The Union Budget 2025–26 identified NMP 2.0 as the second phase of India’s asset monetisation strategy, aiming to unlock the value of operating public infrastructure for sustainable financing.
 
• **NITI Aayog Role:** The report, prepared by **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with infrastructure ministries, outlines a medium-term plan for the period **FY 2026 – FY 2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points: The 5 Stages of Estimation__**

The approach to estimating the monetisation potential under NMP 2.0 follows a structured 5-stage methodology:

 
• **Identification of the Asset Classes:** Selecting specific brownfield assets across 12 sectors (Highways, Railways, etc.) that are ready for monetisation.
 
• **Determination of suitable mode of monetisation:** Choosing between models like **InvITs** (Infrastructure Investment Trusts), **REITs**, or contractual models like **OMT** (Operate-Maintain-Transfer).
 
• **Estimation of monetisation value:** Calculating the potential financial value of individual assets.
 
• **Estimation of ‘Aggregate Monetisation Value’:** Compiling the total value to reach the national target (estimated at **₹16.72 Lakh Crore**).
 
• **Allocation of proceeds from monetisation:** Strategizing how the generated funds will be recycled into new greenfield infrastructure projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Why Option 3 is Incorrect__**

 
• **Ownership vs. Rights:** A core pillar of the National Monetisation Pipeline is that it involves the **transfer of revenue rights** to the private sector for a specific transaction period, not the permanent sale of the asset.
 
• **Land Exclusion:** Under the NMP framework, the **direct permanent sale of public land** is generally excluded, as the primary goal is "Capital Recycling" where the government retains ultimate ownership of the core infrastructure.
 
• **Brownfield Focus:** The pipeline focuses on **de-risked, brownfield assets** that are already operational and generating revenue.

Hepatitis D also spreads in a similar manner, because Hepatitis D virus infection occurs only in persons infected with Hepatitis B virus. Hence, **Statement II is correct**.
 
• **Statement III: **Hepatitis D is not typically transmitted through contaminated food and water. Food-and-water transmission is mainly associated with Hepatitis A and Hepatitis E. Hepatitis A spreads when a person ingests food or water contaminated with faeces of an infected person. Hence, **Statement III is incorrect**.
 
• Therefore, **only one statement is correct**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hepatitis is a broad term meaning **inflammation of the liver**. It may be caused by hepatitis viruses, alcohol, toxins, certain medicines, autoimmune conditions and some other infections. Therefore, every case of hepatitis is not necessarily viral hepatitis.
 
• The five major hepatitis viruses are **Hepatitis A, B, C, D and E**. They differ mainly in their route of transmission, tendency to become chronic, availability of vaccines and risk of long-term complications.

• **Hepatitis A and Hepatitis E** are commonly linked with the **faeco-oral route**, especially unsafe food, unsafe water and poor sanitation.** Hepatitis A usually causes an acute illness, and most infected persons recover completely with lifelong immunity. **
 
• **Hepatitis B** is important because it can spread through **infected blood, semen and other body fluids**, and it may also pass from mother to child during birth. Chronic Hepatitis B can lead to cirrhosis and liver cancer.
 
• **Hepatitis D is unique because it is a defective virus**. It cannot establish infection independently and requires Hepatitis B virus for its life cycle. Therefore, **Hepatitis D infection occurs only in persons who are already infected with Hepatitis B or who acquire Hepatitis B and D together. **
 
• There are two important patterns of Hepatitis D infection. **Co-infection** occurs when a person gets Hepatitis B and Hepatitis D at the same time. **Superinfection** occurs when a person already having chronic **Hepatitis B later acquires Hepatitis D**. Superinfection is usually more dangerous and may accelerate progression to cirrhosis and liver failure.
 
• The Hepatitis B vaccine also helps prevent **Hepatitis D because Hepatitis D depends on Hepatitis B. Thus, vaccination against Hepatitis B is an important preventive measure against both Hepatitis B and Hepatitis D.**

questions.question: How many languages are there in Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
Option **4** is the correct answer: Currently, there are __**22**__ languages approved by the constitution of India.

 
• **Schedule VIII** of the Indian constitution has given recognition to 22 languages.
 
• Initially, there were **14** languages in the eighth schedule of our constitution.
 
• **21st Constitutional Amendment Act (CAA) 1967** added one language (**Sindhi**), **71st CAA, 1992** added 3 (**Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali**).
 
• **92ⁿd CAA od 2003** added **Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali** to the eighth schedule making a total of 22 languages.

**Facts**:

 
• **English and Hindi** are the languages declared by our constitution for transacting business in the Parliament.
 
• **English and Hindi **are the official languages of India.
 
• There is **no national language** of India as mentioned by the constitution of India.
 
• To give constitutional recognition to a language recognition it must be added to the eighth schedule of our constitution by the Constitutional Amendment Act
